name: Question 19
problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(3,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(-1<X<7)=0.8948,$ use the table to find  $\sigma ,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.5\,$ | $\,0.9345\,$ | $\,0.9357\,$ | $\,0.9370\,$ |
| $\,1.6\,$ | $\,0.9463\,$ | $\,0.9474\,$ | $\,0.9484\,$ |
| $\,1.7\,$ | $\,0.9564\,$ | $\,0.9573\,$ | $\,0.9582\,$ |

*Hint: Note that the interval $-1<X<7$ is symmetric about the mean $\mu =3.$*

$\sigma ≈$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, note that the given interval is symmetric about the mean:

$$
P(-1<X<7)=P(3-4<X<3+4)
$$

So, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1<X<7) & =0.8948 \\ 2P(3<X<7) & =0.8948 \\ P(3<X<7) & =0.4474 \\ P(X<7)-P(X<3) & =0.4474 \\ P(X<7)-0.5 & =0.4474 \\ P(X<7) & =0.9474 \\ P(X\le 7) & =0.9474\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 7) & =0.9474 \\ P(Z\le \frac{7-3}{\sigma }) & =0.9474 \\ Φ(\frac{4}{\sigma }) & =0.9474 \\ \frac{4}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.9474)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(1.62)=0.9474\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.9474)=1.62.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{\sigma } & =1.62 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{4}{1.62} \\ \sigma  & ≈2.47.\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
